title: Podcasting
desc: Plan, record, edit, publish and grow a podcast with good audio, honest rights, and a simple way to earn.
outcomes: Explain formats, audiences and the production chain.
Record clean audio and edit with free tools.
task: Plan and publish a three-episode podcast season with show plan, scripts, clean audio, show notes, rights check and listener review.
condition: A phone or mic, free editing software, a quiet room, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Audio is clear with steady levels; every episode has notes and a rights check; episodes publish on a free host; listener data reviewed; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Creators, teachers, small businesses, community groups.
evidence: show plan, 3 episodes, show notes, rights sheet, review
modules: A podcast is a promise to one listener.
One listener, one promise, one format.
A 15-minute weekly farm tips show for small farmers.
A cold open with one surprising fact keeps listeners.
Good sound is the biggest quality factor.
Quiet room, soft surfaces, mic distance of a hand width.
Recording inside a wardrobe of clothes reduces echo.
Cut mistakes, balance levels and remove noise.
Add intro and outro; export in a standard format.
Check on phone speaker and headphones.
Loudness is set so episodes sound equal.
Use only music and clips you may use.
Royalty-free music is credited as required.
Free host and feed to apps.
A square cover image is clear at small size.
Live in at least one app.
Change one thing at a time.
Drop-off at minute 8 leads to shorter segments.
The sponsor tag is read at the start of each episode.
quiz: Hook purpose?
Capture attention. (Covered in module 1: Concept and audience. To pass that module: One page.)
Clipping?
Distorted loud peaks. (Covered in module 2: Script and structure. To pass that module: Timed.)
Mic distance?
About a hand width. (Covered in module 3: Recording. To pass that module: No clipping.)
Rights rule?
Use only what you may. (Covered in module 4: Editing. To pass that module: Levels steady.)
Guest consent?
Required. (Covered in module 5: Rights and ethics. To pass that module: Every item sourced.)
Drop-off?
Where listeners leave. (Covered in module 6: Publish and promote. To pass that module: Live in at least one app.)
Sponsor rule?
Disclose. (Covered in module 7: Listener data. To pass that module: Three findings.)
Why room tone?
Fix gaps. (Covered in module 8: Earn and sustain. To pass that module: Disclosure included.)
Show notes use?
Search and clarity. (Covered in module 8: Earn and sustain. To pass that module: Disclosure included.)
Free host?
Distributes feed. (Covered in module 8: Earn and sustain. To pass that module: Disclosure included.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: social media network building, VR live events, holographic theatre.
local: Music and privacy laws differ by place.
ladder: Concept and audience

L1: learner can name formats. Focus module: Concept and audience (Understand, 3 h). Know who and why. Key points: One listener, one promise, one format. Interview, solo, story or panel. Episode length and schedule.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 15-minute weekly farm tips show. Then set the activity: Write a show plan. Mark against the standard: One page. Check at this level: Hook purpose? Model answer: Capture attention. Formats.
Script and structure
L2: learner knows audio basics. Focus module: Script and structure (Create, 4 h). Plan before you press record. Key points: Hook, body, close. Write the first 30 seconds fully. Time every part.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cold open with one surprising fact. Then set the activity: Script episode one. Mark against the standard: Timed. Check at this level: Clipping? Model answer: Distorted loud peaks. Audio.
Recording
L3: learner can record. Focus module: Recording (Apply, 5 h). Clean sound. Key points: Quiet room, soft surfaces, mic distance of a hand width. Test levels; avoid clipping. Record a room tone.

Teach: open with the worked example. Recording inside a wardrobe of clothes reduces echo. Then set the activity: Record a test. Mark against the standard: No clipping. Check at this level: Mic distance? Model answer: About a hand width. Record.
Editing
L4: learner can edit. Focus module: Editing (Apply, 5 h). Free tools suffice. Key points: Cut mistakes, balance levels, remove noise. Add intro and outro; export in standard format. Keep a backup.

Teach: open with the worked example. Loudness is set so episodes sound equal. Then set the activity: Edit episode one. Mark against the standard: Levels steady. Check at this level: Rights rule? Model answer: Use only what you may. Edit.
Rights and ethics

L5: learner can analyse data. Focus module: Rights and ethics (Evaluate, 3 h). Respect others. Key points: Use only music and clips you have the right to use. Get consent from guests. No harm or false claims.

Teach: open with the worked example. Royalty-free music is credited as required. Then set the activity: Complete a rights sheet. Mark against the standard: Every item sourced. Check at this level: Guest consent? Model answer: Required. Data.
Listener data
L6: learner can lead a team. Focus module: Listener data (Analyse, 3 h). Learn from numbers. Key points: Downloads, drop-off points, replies. Ask for feedback. Change one thing at a time.

Teach: open with the worked example. Drop-off at minute 8 leads to shorter segments. Then set the activity: Review data. Mark against the standard: Three findings. Check at this level: Drop-off? Model answer: Where listeners leave. Team.
Earn and sustain
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Earn and sustain (Evaluate, 3 h). Honest money. Key points: Sponsors, donations, courses, services. Disclose sponsors clearly. Keep a calendar.

Teach: open with the worked example. Sponsor tag is read at start. Then set the activity: Plan income. Mark against the standard: Disclosure included. Check at this level: Sponsor rule? Model answer: Disclose. Peer audit.
